vectors.name: document-model/limits/depth-at-declared-limit-succeeds
vectors.comment: Three levels of nesting (a > b > c) against a declared limit of 3 -- exactly at the boundary, MUST succeed. Nesting is brace-delimited (Sec4.1: indentation is insignificant in OML), not indentation -- confirmed live that the equivalent indentation-only text is a syntax error, not valid input at all.

vectors.name: document-model/limits/depth-one-past-declared-limit-fails
vectors.comment: One level past the same declared limit. declared_max_depth is a vector-local parameter, not Python's reference default of 200 (§2.4 states the numbers are not normative, only the existence of a finite limit and the error family it MUST produce are). A harness runs the implementation under test with its own limit configured to this value for the vector's duration; an implementation exposing no such configuration surface yet -- true of Python today per §2.4 -- reports this vector as skip, not fail, since it cannot be pointed at 3. Either way this pins the rule: exceeding your own declared limit produces document.limit.depth, never truncation, never a different code. Nesting is brace-delimited (Sec4.1), not indentation.

vectors.name: document-model/limits/node-count-at-declared-limit-succeeds
vectors.comment: One node materialized (the root), at a declared node-count limit of 1 -- exactly at the boundary, MUST succeed. The node cap bounds materialized nodes, not depth or edge count within one node (§2.4): a single flat node with any number of sibling edges is still one node.

vectors.name: document-model/limits/node-count-one-past-declared-limit-fails
vectors.comment: Two nodes materialized (root, plus the nested node under `a`) against the same declared limit of 1. declared_max_nodes is vector-local, not Python's reference default of 1,000,000 -- same skip-not-fail caveat as the depth vector above applies to any implementation with no configuration surface for this limit. Nesting is brace-delimited (Sec4.1), not indentation.

vectors.name: document-model/limits/integer-digits-at-declared-limit-succeeds
vectors.comment: Three decimal digits (sign excluded, per §2.4) against a declared limit of 3 -- exactly at the boundary, MUST succeed.

vectors.name: document-model/limits/integer-digits-one-past-declared-limit-fails
vectors.comment: One digit past the same declared limit. declared_max_int_digits is vector-local, not Python's reference default of 4,300 (which itself matches CPython's sys.set_int_max_str_digits). Same skip-not-fail caveat applies.
